choices.text: Nothing: one cold day really does prove the climate is colder
One day is weather, not climate: climate is the pattern of weather over many years
Cold days never happen in a warm climate

questions.explanation: The trap is: A cold day today means the climate is getting colder. Today's weather is not the climate: climate is the pattern of weather over many years, not one cold or hot day.
questions.misconception: A cold day today means the climate is getting colder.
questions.prompt: A pupil says one cold day proves the climate is getting colder. What is wrong with this idea?

choices.text: It sinks down and stays still

questions.explanation: Scene s1: the sun heats the land, the land warms the air above it, and the warm air begins to rise.
questions.prompt: The sun heats the land on a sunny day. What happens to the air just above the warm land?

questions.answer: Cooler air flows in to take the place of the risen warm air, and that moving air is what we feel as wind.
questions.explanation: Scene s2: warm air rises, cool air flows in to fill the space, and the moving air is wind.
questions.prompt: Warm air rises above the heated land. What flows in to take its place, and what do we call that moving air?

questions.answer: High up, the risen warm air cools and gathers into clouds; the drops grow heavy and fall as rain.
questions.explanation: Scene s3: clouds gather, rain falls - cooled air forms clouds and the heavy drops fall back to the ground.
questions.prompt: In your own words, say how clouds and rain form at the end of the heat chain.

choices.text: The weather on one cold day
The pattern of weather over many years

questions.explanation: Climate is the pattern of weather over many years, not one cold or hot day - that is the reteach point of the whole lesson.

subject: geography
title: Weather and climate: heat on the move
